MSFT.rationale: Microsoft presents a strong fundamental case: 18.3% YoY revenue growth on an $82.9B quarterly base, stable 46.3% operating margins, operating cash flow of $46.7B (147% of net income), and a $38B net cash fortress balance sheet. The AI business has reached $37B ARR growing 123% YoY, and Azure is growing 40% YoY, outpacing both AWS and Google Cloud. Valuation has compressed meaningfully — PE of 30.4x sits in the lower quartile of its 25.4x–42.8x one-year range, representing a ~23% drawdown from the 52-week high despite continued fundamental acceleration. The stock is cheaper than it has been for most of the past year on a business that is demonstrably larger and more profitable. However, the earnings yield (3.3%) still sits 115bps below the 10-year Treasury yield (4.45%), leaving the stock rate-sensitive and capping the upside. The $190B capex plan creates real near-term FCF pressure, and Copilot penetration at only 4.4% of the M365 base means the AI monetization thesis is still early. The upcoming Build conference (week of May 28) and Q4 earnings (July 29) provide dated catalysts, and the OpenAI restructuring improves long-term economics despite removing exclusivity. Net constructive but not a screaming bargain — the multiple has compressed but not to trough levels, and the rate headwind is structural.

Upcoming Build conference (week of May 28) with reports of new coding model and AI applications; Q4 earnings July 29 provide near-term catalysts
